prog.transitionInterview: Your first step: meet VAC early in your release to find the right services for you and your family.
prog.disability: Tax-free financial recognition for an illness or injury related to your service, like PTSD, hearing loss or tinnitus.
prog.mentalHealthBenefits: Coverage for treatment of anxiety, depression or trauma while VAC reviews your disability benefit application.
prog.assistance: Talk to a mental health professional any time, free and confidential, for you and your family.
prog.etb: Money for college, university, technical programs or short courses, at the school you choose.
prog.cts: One-on-one career counselling, help with your resume, interview practice and job search.
prog.rehab: Medical, psycho-social and vocational help to adjust to life at home, in your community or at work.
prog.irb: Monthly income while you take part in rehabilitation: 90% of your gross pre-release military salary. Some other income is deducted, but you can earn up to {earnings} a year from work without it affecting the benefit.
prog.vef: Fast money for essentials like food, clothing, shelter or uninsured medical costs.
prog.treatment: Coverage for health care, prescriptions, devices, dental, hearing and vision services.
prog.osiClinics: Assessment and treatment for service-related mental health issues, in person or online, from teams who understand Veterans.
prog.caseManagement: A case manager helps you and your family set goals and coordinate services when things get complex.
prog.vip: Yearly tax-free funding for housekeeping, grounds maintenance, meals, personal care and health support at home.
prog.crb: A tax-free monthly payment to the unpaid caregiver who makes it possible for you to stay at home.
prog.cfis: A tax-free monthly benefit for low-income Veterans, survivors and orphans after the Income Replacement Benefit ends.
prog.vfp: Your family keeps access to Military Family Resource Centres, courses and a coordinator through a medical release.
prog.memberAssistance: Confidential short-term counselling for serving members and their families, any time.
prog.deathBenefit: A one-time, tax-free payment to the spouse or partner and dependent children of a CAF member who dies of a service-related injury or illness.
nav.stat.disability.note: Monthly or as a lump sum
nav.stat.mhb.note: Starts when VAC gets your application
nav.stat.irb.note: A year: the pre-tax floor. Work income up to {earnings} a year isn’t deducted
nav.stat.vef.note: To a decision, once your application is complete
nav.stat.crb.note: A month, paid to your caregiver
nav.stat.cfis.note: A month, tax-free. Rate set in {since}; adjusted every three months.
reason.serviceRelated: If your illness or injury is related to your service.
reason.sixYears: Needs at least 6 years (2,191 days) of paid service and an honourable release.
reason.rehab: While you take part in VAC’s Rehabilitation Program.
reason.crb: When you need daily care from an unpaid caregiver because of the condition your disability benefit covers.
reason.cfis: When your Income Replacement Benefit ended in the last 6 months, your household income is low, and you’re looking for work or in Career Transition Services.
reason.deathBenefit: When the death is from a service-related injury or illness, within 30 days of the injury or of the illness starting. After that, support comes through disability benefits.
reason.vefFamily: For current spouses and partners of Veterans, and survivors and orphans of Veterans or CAF members.
mh.title: Mental health support
mh.subtitle: For Veterans, CAF members, RCMP and families
mh.error.title: We couldn’t load this right now
mh.error.body: You can talk to a mental health professional any time at {phone}. It’s free and confidential.
mh.crisis.title: In danger right now? Call 911.
mh.crisis.body: Thinking about suicide, or worried about someone? Call or text 9-8-8, any time.
mh.now.assistance.1: A bilingual mental health professional answers, trained in crisis and suicide intervention.
mh.now.assistance.2: Up to 20 hours of support per issue, for you, your family and your caregiver. No need to apply.
mh.now.assistance.3: They can refer you to a professional near you, usually within 5 working days.
mh.now.memberAssistance.1: Short-term counselling for Regular Force members and their families, and some Reservists.
mh.now.memberAssistance.2: Voluntary and confidential: stress, family, work, alcohol or drugs, harassment.
mh.now.memberAssistance.3: They can refer you to a mental health professional near you.
mh.now.familyLine.1: Trained counsellors offer information, support, referrals and help in a crisis.
mh.now.familyLine.2: They help you and your family find national and local services for military families.
mh.now.familyLine.3: You can also visit the Military Family Resource Centre on your base or wing.
mh.hours.weekdays: Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 4:30 local time
mh.hours.transition-group: Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern
mh.sec.peer: Talk to someone who’s been there
mh.row.osiss.name: Operational Stress Injury Social Support (OSISS)
mh.row.osiss.body: Peer support from people who understand operational stress injuries, for members, Veterans and their families. The CAF Transition Group can connect you.
mh.row.sosi.name: Support for Operational Stress Injury (SOSI)
mh.row.sosi.body: A national peer support network for RCMP Veterans and members having a hard time because of their service.
mh.row.osiClinics.name: OSI clinics
mh.row.osiClinics.body: Assessment and treatment for service-related mental health issues, in person or online. No application needed.
mh.row.mentalHealthBenefits.name: Mental Health Benefits
mh.row.mentalHealthBenefits.body: Treatment for anxiety, depression or trauma is covered from the day VAC receives your disability benefit application.
mh.row.cafClinic.name: Your CAF medical centre
mh.row.cafClinic.body: Walk in to your local CAF medical centre for crisis care. After hours, go to a hospital emergency department, or call 911 in an emergency.
mh.row.familyLine.name: Family Information Line
mh.row.familyLine.body: Confidential counselling, information and crisis support for CAF members, Veterans and their families.
mh.row.assistance.name: VAC Assistance Service
mh.row.assistance.body: A mental health professional, free and confidential, for families of Veterans and former RCMP members. Families of serving members reach the CF Member Assistance Program at the same number.
mh.row.vfp.name: Veteran Family Program
mh.row.vfp.body: Transition support for families of members who are medically releasing or released, at any Military Family Resource Centre.
mh.footnote: Nothing you choose here is saved or sent anywhere.

results.regularOnly: Recruiting allowances and signing bonuses are for the Regular Force (full-time) only.

careers.q.hoursHint: Full-time is the Regular Force. Part-time is the Reserve.
nav.stat.mhb.noteReleasing: If you applied for disability benefits before you release
reason.etbWindow: Apply within 10 years of your release. Released between April 1, 2006 and March 31, 2018? You have until April 1, 2028.
reason.etbWindowReleasing: You’ll have 10 years from your release to apply.
stat.payNotePartTime: A month, the Regular Force rate. Ask a recruiter about Reserve pay
stat.leaveNoteFull: Days a year to start, 25 after 5 years of service
stat.leaveNotePartTime: Days a year, for members who serve full-time
prog.crbFamily: A tax-free monthly payment to you, as the unpaid caregiver of a Veteran who needs daily care. The Veteran applies, and you fill out one section.
prog.vfpFamily: Through a medical release and after, your Military Family Resource Centre offers courses and a coordinator who helps plan your family’s next steps.
prog.osiClinicsFamily: Assessment and treatment for the Veteran’s service-related mental health issues. Family members may also take part in some of the clinic’s services.
reason.serviceRelatedFamily: If the Veteran’s illness or injury is related to their service.
reason.crbFamily: When the Veteran needs ongoing daily care because of the condition their disability benefit covers, and you are over 18 and unpaid.
nav.stat.crb.noteFamily: A month, paid directly to you
nav.q.serviceFamily: Is the Veteran’s illness or injury related to their service?
prog.vipSurvivor: Yearly tax-free funding toward housekeeping and grounds maintenance, so you can stay in your own home.
reason.vipSurvivor: For the survivor of a Second World War or Korean War Veteran who received, or was eligible for, a Disability Pension or the War Veterans Allowance.
reason.vipSurvivorCare: You were their main caregiver, unpaid, for at least a year, and you have a health-related need for these services.
reason.vipSurvivorIncome: You live in Canada and have a low income (you receive the Guaranteed Income Supplement) or a disability (you receive the Disability Tax Credit).
reason.vipSurvivorCaregiver: If the Veteran was already receiving VIP services, you apply as their primary caregiver instead.
prog.cfisSurvivor: A tax-free monthly benefit for low-income survivors and orphans of Canadian Armed Forces Veterans.
reason.cfisSurvivor: When your income is low and your Earnings Loss Benefit for Survivors has ended, or the Veteran was receiving this benefit when they died.
reason.cfisSurvivorDeadline: If the death was not related to service, apply within 6 months of the end of the month the Veteran died. There is no time limit if it was.
